pages.text:
Titus has a satchel with a scroll tucked inside,
And a question that's too big and too good to hide.
Today's little question is curly and thin:
"Why did Daniel keep praying? Let's go and begin!"

Now Daniel loved God, and here's what he'd do —
Three times every day, he would pray. It was true!
By the window he'd kneel with his hands open wide.
Morning, noon, and at night, with God right by his side.

But some men didn't like him. They whispered a plan.
"Let's make a new rule for each woman and man!
For thirty whole days — not a prayer, not a peep!"
And the king signed it down. Oh, that rule cut deep.

Did Daniel stop praying? Oh no. Not one bit!
By the very same window, he knelt down and sit.
He talked to his God just the same as before —
Morning, noon, and at night. Even more.

The king was so sad. He had made a mistake!
But a rule is a rule, and a rule doesn't break.
"To the den with the lions," the king had to say.
"May your God, whom you serve, keep you safe till the day."

They rolled a big stone. It went CLUNK. It went BOOM.
And inside was dark, and inside was room
For lions — big lions with paws like a drum.
Titus whispered, "Oh my. Here we come."

The lions were huge. They had manes like the sun.
And Daniel just knelt there. He didn't run.
He prayed in the dark, the same way he'd begun —
Morning, noon, and at night. Every one.

Then God sent an angel — and what do you think?

God shut the lions' mouths! (ROAR!)
God shut the lions' mouths! (ROAR!)
Not a nibble, not a bite, not a chomp, not a chew —
God shut the lions' mouths! It's true!

At sunrise the king ran as fast as he could.
"Oh Daniel! Oh Daniel! Was your God good?"
He rolled back the stone and he called down the hall —
"Are you there? Are you safe? Are you well after all?"

And Daniel called back, "I'm alive! I'm all right!
My God sent an angel to guard me all night.
The lions were gentle. Not one came near."
And the whole kingdom shouted a great big cheer!

So why did Daniel keep praying? Now Titus could see:
Not because it was easy. Not because it was free.
But because talking to God is the best thing to do —
When it's hard, when it's dark, when the lions are too.

Now sing it with Titus! Let's give it a shout —
That's what this whole wonderful story's about!

God shut the lions' mouths! (ROAR!)
God shut the lions' mouths! (ROAR!)
